about.text: Bovine Lacto Transfer Technique Optimizer: a solution of nonfat dry milk, usually 5 % in buffer, used in laboratories since 1984 to block the empty places on a blot membrane, so that antibodies or probes stick only to what they are meant to find.

links.name: Gene Analysis Techniques (1984), Johnson et al.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: No cooking is involved: the skimmed milk powder is just stirred into buffer. The proteins coat the membrane so that antibodies bind only to the target.

facts.v: Mainly casein, which sticks to every free spot on the membrane
Purified BSA, ovalbumin or gelatin: costly
Casein is a phosphoprotein, so milk is unsuitable with phospho-specific antibodies
